title: Josh Giuliano’s TIFF Slasher ‘River’ Selling to Universal and Blumhouse Atomic Monster for North of $10 Million
description: In the first major deal of the Toronto Film Festival, Joshua Giuliano’s slasher film “River” is in talks to be acquired by Universal Pictures and Bl
body:
In the first major deal of the Toronto Film Festival, Joshua Giuliano’s slasher film “River” is in talks to be acquired by Universal Pictures and Blumhouse Atomic Monster, Variety has confirmed. Giuliano’s film was originally backed by Independent Film Company and Shudder, but the companies are now closing a deal to sell distribution rights to the debut feature for north of $10 million after its TIFF world premiere.

	The slasher is written and directed by Giuliano and stars Jane Levy (“Evil Dead”), Jessica Rothe (“Happy Death Day”) and Max Mattern (“Devil in Disguise: John Wayne”) as estranged siblings who reunite in their hometown after their father’s death. According to the official synopsis, when they set out to scatter his ashes at a favorite spot on a remote river, their boat breaks down and the trip devolves into a waking nightmare. Dane DiLiegro (“Prey”) also stars.
	

	“River” is produced by Nick Antosca, Alex Hedlund and Steven Schneider and executive produced by Roy Lee, Ben Ross, Matt Brodlie, Jonathan Kier, Jeffrey Tinnell, Robert Tinnell and Jason Blum.


	Sam Zimmerman, who now leads the indies slate at Blumhouse Atomic Monster, had a relationship Giuliano during his time at Shudder.

	Last week, Blumhouse Atomic Monster, Divie/Conquer and Spooky Pictures signed on for Giuliano’s next film, “Occupant,” with Focus Features distributing. The filmmaker, who was part of the American Film Institute’s directing program, has won awards for his short films at genre festivals including Fantasia, Fantastic Fest and FrightFest.
	

	Giuliano is repped by CAA, Kaplan Perrone Entertainment and Marios Rush.

	News of the deal was first reported by IndieWire.

title: Henry Winkler Refused to Let ABC Change ‘Happy Days’ Title to ‘Fonzie’s Happy Days’ Because ‘It Would Be a Slap in the Face’ to Co-Stars
description: Henry Winkler opened up on the latest episode of “In Depth With Graham Bensinger” about refusing to let ABC executives change the name of “Happy Day
body:
Henry Winkler opened up on the latest episode of “In Depth With Graham Bensinger” about refusing to let ABC executives change the name of “Happy Days” to “Fonzie’s Happy Days” due to the explosive popularity of his character. Winkler starred as Arthur “Fonzie” Fonzarelli on all 11 seasons and 255 episodes of the iconic ABC sitcom. He debuted as a recurring role before being upped to a series regular during the show’s second season because of how beloved the Fonz became with fans. 
	

	“Before ‘Happy Days’, ABC was in the basement. It was the last of the three networks,” Winkler said. “And [ABC president Leonard Goldenson] came to my office, my dressing room, and he said, ‘First of all, I would like to call the show “Fonzie’s Happy Days.” We’re thinking of changing the title.’ And I said, ‘Sir, I’m really asking you not to do that’… We were really soaring in the in the ratings. It wasn’t broken. This would be a slap in the face. Why change the title if it is working so magnificently?”


	Winkler was also concerned about keeping tensions among the ensemble cast at bay. According to the actor, Ron Howard was already annoyed with Fonz becoming the show’s breakout character and felt he was being “overshadowed” by him. Howard played the show’s original lead character Richie Cunningham, leaving “Happy Days” after seven seasons. 

	“[Ron] said, ‘Look, it hurt my feelings. You’re not doing anything to hurt my feelings. You’re really good and you’re good for the show. It’s helping the show. So I put all of that together and that’s the way it is.’ And we never talked about it again,” Winkler said of Howard’s annoyances. 
	

	Regardless, Winkler wanted to keep the peace among the cast and turned down the title change because “we can’t do [the show] if we are resentful or angry of each other.” The actor also turned down Goldenson’s offer to spin off Fonz into his own series because “I have no idea if I’d have a chemistry with new people.” Winkler told the ABC boss: “I don’t think I can do my own show. I think I’m very happy right where I am with this extraordinary family.”

	Howard revealed in a career-spanning Vulture interview last year that while he grew comfortable over time with Winkler’s Fonz becoming the star of “Happy Days,” he drew a line at having the show be retitled. Howard even threatened to leave the show if they changed the title.

	“I never, ever challenged what they were doing creatively. It made perfect sense that you’d build this Fonzie character and maximize that,” Howard said. “But the optics of now being in a show called ‘Fonzie’s Happy Days,’ my ego wouldn’t allow for that. I wasn’t bluffing. I would’ve left. And my contract, I’m sure, had no clause connected to titles. They could have said, ‘Fuck you. We changed the title, and we expect you to show up Monday morning.’ But thank God for great bosses. Garry Marshall said, ‘If you’re not cool with it …’”

	“I later found out Henry himself thought it was a terrible idea,” Howard continued. “I think the position I took made it easy for both Garry and Henry to also say, ‘No, let’s not do that.’ Years later, Henry said they were ready to do a spinoff and other things for Fonzie and he just said, ‘Why fix it if it’s not broken? My success depends on the ensemble I’m in.’”

title: Robert Kraft Defends Banning Macklemore From Ed Sheeran Tour After ‘Free Palestine’ Comments: ‘We Do Not Provide a Platform for Hate Speech’
description: New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft has issued a statement defending his decision to create what amounts to a ban on rapper Macklemore performin
body:
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft has issued a statement defending his decision to create what amounts to a ban on rapper Macklemore performing in support of Ed Sheeran at a number of stadiums following the rapper’s comments regarding Palestine, which took place at concerts in New Jersey on Sept. 4 and 5. 

	In his comment on being removed from the tour, Macklemore placed the place the blame on Kraft, saying that the billionaire rallied other stadium owners to refuse to allow Macklemore to perform at their venues.
	

	In his response, Kraft says he would “welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts.” There seemed to be some confusion in Kraft’s office regarding the statement, as it took nearly an hour to confirm its authenticity to Variety. Macklemore and Sheeran did not immediately respond to Kraft’s comment; Sheeran has remained quiet about the incident since it initially took place. 


	In his statement, Kraft says: “Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech. Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line.

	“This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real. But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas, a United States and globally (including Canada, European Union, United Kingdom, and Japan) designated terrorist organization whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike. I agree with Macklemore. Too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering, but only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate. Over many decades, I have directed resources to Palestine and created athletic and entrepreneurial opportunities for Palestinians who I admire and respect. Standing with the Palestinian people and standing against Hamas, antisemitism and hate should not be mutually exclusive.
	

	“Much of my time and attention for the last decade has been focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed. I have tremendous respect for Ed and his music, particularly his unique ability to bring people together and spread joy, and I have always been proud to welcome him and his fans to Gillette Stadium.

	“I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same – peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate.” – Robert Kraft

	In a long social media post earlier on Monday, Macklemore said in part: “Last Monday, in the middle of all the media attention surrounding Pink and what I said at MetLife, Ed told me that Robert Kraft called him. We were scheduled to play Gillette Stadium later this month, which is owned by the Kraft Group. Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium. Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.

	“Ed was in a fucked up position. He knew it. His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before. He told me that the words “Free Palestine” and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with. I told him that if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood. But he couldn’t get past his public facing, “I don’t take sides.”

	“And I get why people don’t. Taking a side can cost you. Money, brand deals, sponsorships, festivals, private shows, relationships and access. I’ve lost all of those things. But there is no neutral position between the oppressor and the oppressed. When one side has the bombs and bottomless financial and military support from America, refusing to take a side doesn’t leave you in the middle.”

	Concert promoter Messina Touring Group released a statement early Monday bout dropping Macklemore from the tour on Sept. 14.
	

	“As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans,” the statement read. “After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates.”

title: ‘Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ Star Mikayla Matthews Steps Away From Series Amid Taylor Frankie Paul Scandal: ‘Feels Wrong and Unethical’
description: “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” cast member Mikayla Matthews has announced that she is stepping away from the reality series “after hearing some
body:
“The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” cast member Mikayla Matthews has announced that she is stepping away from the reality series “after hearing some news” she found upsetting, seemingly related to the ongoing scandal surrounding Taylor Frankie Paul.

	“I will not be continuing the show at this moment,” she wrote in an Instagram caption. “I’ve said from the beginning of this that I’m not comfortable being a part of something that continues to platform behavior I don’t agree especially given my own experience growing up in a home with multiple forms of abuse. There’s no amount of money worth going against my morals or changing the stance I’ve had since I first saw and heard the things that made me feel this strongly. And for me personally, continuing to directly profit from this behavior feels wrong and unethical. It feels like a disservice to the children, everyone’s healing and the millions of people watching.”
	

	“This show has been a huge part of my life and has helped me provide for my family,” Matthews continued. “I’m so grateful for the experience, and will continue sharing my story, my health and advocating for myself and others. This shouldn’t be ‘relatable’ or entertainment in anyway. Supporting an ADULT doesn’t mean constantly making excuses for toxic behavior while giving unconditional sympathy and grace with zero accountability or change. I was in that enabling cycle for years, and I’m not going to be a part of that again! Love you all.”


	Matthews’ post comes days after the release of “Mormon Wives” Season 5, which saw her and Paul get into multiple arguments after Matthews pointed out chaotic patterns in Paul’s dating life, with Paul finding Matthews to be harsh and judgmental. The conflicts depicted took place before TMZ published footage from a domestic incident between Paul and her ex-boyfriend Dakota Mortensen in which Paul threw metal chairs at him. The ensuing scandal has involved domestic violence allegations from both parties, mutual restraining orders and a custody battle, as well as the cancellation of Paul’s “Bachelorette” season. In the months since, Matthews has been vocal online about her continued objections to Paul’s behavior.
	

	Season 6 of “Mormon Wives” is currently in production, though it is unclear whether or how much Matthews will appear in it. Her castmates Mayci Neeley and Layla Taylor both left comments of support on her announcement.

title: MoreThan Films Acquires Serville Poblete’s Buzzy Toronto Hangout Comedy ‘Sunburn’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: International sales agency MoreThan Films has acquired the rights to “Sunburn,” by award-winning director Serville Poblete, ahead of its world premi
body:
International sales agency MoreThan Films has acquired the rights to “Sunburn,” by award-winning director Serville Poblete, ahead of its world premiere as part of the Centrepiece strand of the Toronto International Film Festival. The agency will handle international sales, with Julien Levesque from Gersh handling domestic sales.

	“Sunburn” is set in St. James Town, a high-rise community in Toronto, over the course of a citywide blackout that shuts down phone networks on one of the hottest days recorded in the city. There, a group of kids roams their neighborhood trying to escape the heat as their youth begins to slip away. The film stars Joshua Obra (“Settle Down”), Dashawn Blackwood (“Scaring Women at Night”), Arianna Shannon (“Plan B”) and Milan Deng (“Trap”).
	

	“Serville Poblete is one of the most exciting emerging voices in Canadian cinema today,” Lidia Damatto, co-founder of MoreThan Films, tells Variety. “We were immediately drawn to his distinctive aesthetic and his ability to transform a single summer day into a rich portrait of a community rarely represented on screen.”


	“‘Sunburn’ is a deeply authentic and vibrant mosaic of coming-of-age stories that capture the energy, humor, and uncertainty of youth with remarkable warmth and specificity,” she goes on. “The film is both intimate and expansive, celebrating the beauty of everyday moments while evoking the emotional intensity of adolescence. While firmly rooted in Toronto’s St. James Town community, the film speaks to universal experiences of friendship, identity and belonging, making it a title we believe will resonate strongly with audiences around the world.”
	



	

					Courtesy of MoreThan Films
	



	Serville Poblete is a Filipino-Canadian screenwriter and film director from Toronto. His short documentary “King’s Court” premiered at Hot Docs 2025 and was nominated for a 2026 Canadian Screen Award. His latest short, “In the Morning Sun,” won the Grand Jury Prize at SXSW 2026 and is currently on the festival circuit and is eligible for consideration for the Academy Awards. Serville was selected for the TIFF Next Wave at this year’s festival. “Sunburn” is featured in Variety’s TIFF 2026: 20 International Titles to Track selection.

	“Making a movie about my neighbourhood with so many amazing collaborators felt like summer camp. We had so much fun making it,” says Poblete. “I’m so excited to partner with MoreThanFilms and Gersh to share this project with the world and offer that same warmth to audiences. It’s something I feel the world needs right now.”

	“Sunburn” is written and directed by Serville Poblete (“In the Morning Sun”), executive produced by Neil Champagne (“Blue Heron,” “Good One”), Ryan Bobkin (“Infinity Pool”), Veronica Diaferia (“Blue Heron,” “Good One”) and Sara Eolin (“Blue Heron,” “Good One”), with cinematography by Christian Bielz (“This is Not a Test”).

title: Tribeca Award Winner ‘Labrador – Autopsy of Silence’ Sells to TLA Releasing for the U.S. and the U.K. (EXCLUSIVE)
description: International sales house H264 has sold Rodrigue Jean’s “Labrador – Autopsy of Silence” to TLA Releasing for the U.S. and the U.K. The deal follows
body:
International sales house H264 has sold Rodrigue Jean’s “Labrador – Autopsy of Silence” to TLA Releasing for the U.S. and the U.K. The deal follows the film’s world premiere at the Tribeca Festival, where it won three awards, including best international narrative feature.

	At Tribeca, the film also received the awards for best cinematography, presented to Mathieu Laverdière, and best performance in an international narrative feature, awarded to Christopher Angatookalook.
	

	The film is produced by Patricia Bergeron, Cédric Bourdeau and Rodrigue Jean at Transmar Films.


	In the film, a cargo ship embarks on its final voyage of the year to resupply Inuit communities in the far north of Canada. During a storm off the coast of Labrador, the ship’s cook is found murdered in his cabin. With no way to identify the culprit among the 20 crew members, suspicion falls on Alupa, an Inuit mechanic and close friend of the victim.

	“Against the vast and haunting landscapes of Labrador, the film subverts familiar narrative conventions to explore questions of race, class and sexual identity, revealing a story of remarkable emotional and thematic depth,” H264 said.

	H264 will release the film theatrically in Canada during winter 2027.

	In 1989, Jean directed his first short film, “La Déroute,” followed by the documentary “La Voix des rivières” and the short film “La Mémoire de l’eau.” Two dramatic feature films came soon after: “Full Blast” in 1999 and “Yellowknife” in 2001. Next came the documentaries “Living on the Edge” in 2006 and “Men for Sale” in 2008. “Lost Song,” his third feature film, won the best Canadian feature film award at Toronto in 2008.
	

	He then spent several years directing documentaries with the film collective Groupe Épopée. In 2014, “Love in the Time of Civil War” premiered at Toronto. In 2020, he directed “The Acrobat,” his fifth feature film. In 2022, he co-directed “2012/Through the Heart,” marking the 10th anniversary of the major 2012 student strike in Quebec.

title: How British Comedy Show ‘Mock the Week’ Found New Life on TLC After BBC Cancellation: ‘Absence Makes the Heart Grow Fonder’
description: When long-running BBC comedy show “Mock the Week” returned to television screens after a three-year hiatus this past spring, fans may have noticed s
body:
When long-running BBC comedy show “Mock the Week” returned to television screens after a three-year hiatus this past spring, fans may have noticed some changes: not only was the show longer and “looser” but it was also airing on TLC, the Warner Bros. Discovery-owned network.

	“It was also a surprise for me that it was TLC,” says comedian Rhys James, a regular on the series. “The first episode back was just loads of jokes about ‘Where are we?’ ‘Where have we woken up out of this coma?’ but TLC were well up for having a laugh about that.”
	

	Created by Dan Patterson and Mark Leveson in 2005, “Mock the Week” originally debuted on the BBC, where it spent 17 years until it was axed in 2022 due to budget cuts. But this past February the satirical news show (think “SNL’s” Weekend Update but more off the cuff) finally returned with a new length — 45 minutes instead of 30, excluding ad breaks — and slightly different feel after it was resurrected by TLC.


	“I sort of expected it to be wildly different, but it’s not,” says comedian and fellow regular Angela Barnes, who made her first appearance on the show in 2014. “The set feels like home.”

	Not only was the set largely the same but so was host Dara Ó Briain, who has been the face of “Mock the Week” since it launched in the pre-iPhone era. “It has been a journey,” Ó Briain says of the two decades he’s worked on the show.

	With such a venerable IP, it may have seemed nabbing the show from under the BBC’s nose was a no-brainer but Patterson admits there were never any guarantees “Mock the Week” would return to screens after it was axed. Hopes that Channel 4 or U.K. TV might pick it up fell through, as did a U.S. version for Amazon, “So we sat there for a long time without it,” he says. 
	

	By the time TLC (formerly The Learning Channel) finally called, he was doubtful they’d make a real offer. But not only was it real, they revealed they wanted to relaunch TLC as a free-to-air comedy and entertainment-focused channel with “Mock the Week” as their flagship show. “It was like, ‘Let me think about that. [It’s a] yes,’” Patterson says without missing a beat. (He adds a U.S. version is still in discussion).

	For TLC, a venerable IP with a built-in audience might have seemed like an obvious choice, but Graham Lafferty, SVP for content strategy & networks for WBD U.K. & Ireland, say it was “more risky than it may have looked” since they wouldn’t be able to deliver “BBC numbers” in terms of ratings (the BBC being the most prominent broadcaster in the U.K.) and the format would need to change slightly to accommodate commercial breaks (as the BBC is publicly funded it has no commercials). But with the show’s proven audience and the fact that news viewing is “through the roof” more generally, a satirical news discussion show was deemed worth the risk.

	In a way, the three-year hiatus was also helpful. “I do think absence makes the heart grow fonder,” says Patterson, pointing out that if the show had been picked up just a few months after being canceled on the BBC, people might have been more negative about it. “It just looks like we’re taking their leftovers,” he says. “Whereas with this, we’re not sloppy seconds.”

	The ratings have borne that out. “Mock the Week” Season 1, which launched in February and ran for nine episodes (the season finale was a special), peaked with 337,000 viewers for episode 5, more than the highest-rated episode of “SNL U.K.,” which launched the same weekend that “Mock the Week” wrapped. Both shows returned for a second season this past weekend: “SNL U.K.” on Saturday Sept. 12 and “Mock the Week” on Sunday Sept. 13. They will both air weekly, on Sky and TLC respectively, although “SNL U.K.” has a number of hiatus weeks built in.

	Interestingly, Lafferty says it isn’t just the viewing figures for “Mock the Week” but also the audience profile that ticks the right boxes, given TLC is a commercial channel that relies on ad sales. In fact, he was so happy with the results of the first season he quickly ordered a summer special plus four more seasons, taking the show through to Season 5 in 2027. “It is hard these days to cut through,” Lafferty says. “So if you have something successful, double down on it.”
	

	The commercials are also why the show was extended to around 45 minutes from 30, which has subtly changed its rhythm, mostly for the better, the comedians agree. “I think it’s got looser,” says James. “By looser I mean more conversational. It goes with the flow a bit more, people are a bit more present.”

	Patterson agrees, although said he had a few sleepless nights about the extra 15 minutes before they launched. “I thought it worked at 30 minutes but actually, necessity being what it is, we had to expand it, and I think that’s worked well,” he explains. “Partly because the whole show breathes a little bit more.”

	That one change has also had the knock-on effect of making the show more collegiate. James, Ó Briain and Barnes all say that when it first started, “Mock the Week” had a reputation for predominantly male comedians talking over each other as they each tried to get in their best jokes. That has now dissipated almost entirely. As well as the longer format, James puts it down to the fact most comedians now have podcasts, so they’re better at listening, while Ó Briain thinks it might be age and experience that have simply made them more mellow. 

	Whatever the reason, “it just feels like a better show for it,” says Barnes. “Just more balanced, a different energy, and it isn’t that sort of alpha male fest that it used to be.” (The show also features more female comedians).

	That collegiate feeling may also stem from the fact there’s currently something of a new dawn for comedy on television, with the return of “Mock the Week,” the launch of “SNL U.K.” earlier this year and the success of “L.O.L: Last One Laughing” on Prime Video. TLC in particular is building its slate around comedy, and recently commissioned a host of new shows including a Top Trumps-themed panel show hosted by comedian Katherine Ryan and a second season of “Unacceptable,” which is fronted by Ed Gamble and was renewed for a second season before the first had even launched.

	Ó Briain says he’s witnessed the repeated waxing and waning of comedy commissions throughout his career but even he has been surprised by the strength of feeling surrounding the return of “Mock the Week,” particularly from TLC itself. “Their enthusiasm is incredibly infectious,” he says. “And the audience are happy to see us back. So it’s a very positive thing.”

schema.headline: How British Comedy Show ‘Mock the Week’ Found New Life on TLC After BBC Cancellation: ‘Absence Makes the Heart Grow Fonder’

body:
With the 78th Emmy Awards well underway, it’s officially TV’s biggest night — which means the stars are hitting the red carpet in their Monday best. 
Heading into the evening, HBO Max’s medical drama “The Pitt” leads with 25 nominations, followed closely by “Hacks,” also from the streamer, with 24. (That number made Emmy history, making the fifth season of the show not only the most nominated final season of a comedy in the award program’s history, but the most nominated season of a comedy ever.) 
Following closely behind is Apple TV’s horror comedy hit “Window’s Bay” with 19 nominations, and Apple TV’s “Pluribus” with 18. NBC’s “Saturday Night Live” leads with 11 nominations on the broadcast network side. 
Sterling K. Brown (“Paradise”), Gary Oldman (“Slow Horses”), Mark Ruffalo (“Task”), Rufus Sewell (“The Diplomat”) and Noah Wyle (“The Pitt”) are all nominated for the Emmy Award for best actor in a drama series. In the lead actress in a drama series category, the nominees include Carrie Coon (“The Gilded Age”), Chase Infiniti (“The Testaments”), Keri Russell (“The Diplomat”), Rhea Seehorn (“Pluribus”) and Zendaya (“Euphoria”).  
For best supporting actor in a drama series, “The Pitt” stars Patrick Ball, Shawn Hatosy and Gerran Howell are all nominated, alongside Billy Crudup (“The Morning Show”), Jack Lowden (“Slow Horses”), Tom Pelphrey (“Task”) and Carlos-Manuel Vesga (“Pluribus”).  The ladies of “The Pitt” also lead in nominations for best supporting actress in a drama series: Taylor Deardon, Fiona Dourif, Katherine LaNasa and Sepideh Moafi earned nods for Season 2. Also nominated are Allison Janney (“The Diplomat”), Julianne Nicholson (“Paradise”) and Karolina Wydra (“Pluribus”).

	Final Emmy Predictions in 116 Categories: HBO Max Poised to Dominate With ‘The Pitt’ as ‘Widow’s Bay’ and ‘Hacks’ Chase Opposite All-Time Records
	Awards Circuit Column: Who will win, could win and should win the coveted statuettes from the Television Academy's annual honoring in the best of television.
	



			
			
	
						

									Getty / Apple TV / HBO Max / Netflix 
	
					


							
		

	Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change in response to buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.



	

					Mariska Hargitay
									Michael Schwartz for Variety
	




	Primetime Emmys Predictions Commentary All Categories (Updated: Aug. 29, 2026): “The tribe has spoken.” For the first time in a while, the Emmy race feels genuinely quite settled in the drama race, while the comedy field has a legitimate insurgent, and the limited series category is anyone’s to lose. The ceremony could be a nail-biter. HBO Max’s medical drama and last year’s reigning drama champion “The Pitt” turned a real-time gimmick into the network’s defining series of the year. Apple TV’s horror hit “Widow’s Bay” bulldozed its way into the comedy conversation. At the same time, Netflix’s anthology series “Beef” returned to the fold to take on HBO’s murder-mystery “DTF St. Louis.”

	If the final predictions hold, the same year “Hacks” set the all-time comedy nomination record with 24 — surpassing the 23-nom mark “The Studio” tied with “The Bear” just last year — the Katie Dippold-created horror gem “Widow’s Bay” is projected to win an astounding 15 Emmys, including outstanding comedy series. That would make it the most awarded comedy series in a single year, breaking the record “The Studio” set only last year with 13.

	So where does that leave “Hacks?” The fifth and final season of Jean Smart’s Deborah Vance is projected for a single win — a record-setting eighth acting Emmy for Smart — while losing everywhere else. But the margin is razor-thin, and it points at a not-so-great possible record that could be set. If Lisa Kudrow pulls off what many consider to be impossible and eeks out a lead comedy actress win for the final season of “The Comeback” — denying Smart in the one category “Hacks” is otherwise projected to take — and if the show is blanked across the Creative Arts categories as well, the beloved farewell would back into a brutal headline: the most Emmy losses in a single season in history, surpassing the 21 that “The Handmaid’s Tale” lost in 2021.

	That shouldn’t bum out HBO Max too much, because the network is still projected to dominate the nights overall. “The Pitt” is expected to grow on its freshman tally of five to as many as seven, repeating in drama series and for Noah Wyle, Katherine LaNasa and casting. 

	The limited race looks tighter — HBO’s “DTF St. Louis” is most notably in play — but the second season of Netflix’s anthology “Beef” should squeak it out with six wins, helped by projected acting victories for Oscar Isaac and Carey Mulligan.

	Thanks to a new “area award” format — voters now judge each nominee against an approval threshold rather than picking one winner — the variety series category can crown more than one show. That could hand a beloved farewell to Stephen Colbert, whose “Late Show” won its first Emmy only last year and signs off in 2026, while simultaneously delivering a long-denied first series trophy to Jimmy Kimmel after a year spent tangling with the president and the F.C.C. In this category, in this format, they don’t have to beat each other.

	In other variety categories: “The Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show Starring Bad Bunny” is expected to become the most-awarded Super Bowl halftime show in Emmy history, surpassing the 2022 Dr. Dre/Snoop Dogg/Eminem LVI show, which won three. It would also be the first Spanish-language program to win variety special (live) — and Bad Bunny’s first Emmy.

	In variety special (pre-recorded), Taylor Swift is expected to win her first competitive Emmy — as a producer of her Disney+ “Eras Tour” special — even as her other awards ambitions play out well beyond television. Her “Toy Story 5″ song “I Knew It, I Knew You” is an early Oscar hopeful in the best original song race, while her album, “The Life of a Showgirl” will be seeking Grammy Awards consideration this cycle. Swift has technically been an Emmy winner since 2015, when “AMEX Unstaged: Taylor Swift Experience” took the juried prize for original interactive program. But a pre-recorded win would be her first competitive Emmy, chipping the asterisk off an EGOT-aspiring résumé.

	While CBS’ “Survivor,” coming off its landmark 50th season, looked like it could finally win its first statue for competition program, Peacock’s “The Traitors” appears poised to edge it out, though it’s close.

	A handful of races remain in flux, which only adds pressure to an evening emceed by Emmy winner (and Variety cover star) Mariska Hargitay, likely to become the first person to hold Emmy wins for acting (thanks “Law and Order”) and documentary, if she wins either doc series or director for “My Mom Jayne.”

	The Creative Arts ceremonies honoring the artisans, plus the Governors Gala, take place Sept. 5-6. The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards air Sept. 14 on NBC.

title: Mary Jo Buttafuoco Reveals Breast Cancer Battle, Undergoing Radiation
description:
Mary Jo Buttafuoco
                          I'm Battling Breast Cancer
body:
Mary Jo Buttafuoco
                          I'm Battling Breast Cancer
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 14, 2026
                            1:00 PM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Author and motivational speaker Mary Jo Buttafuoco has breast cancer, TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Mary tells TMZ ... "I recently found a lump in my left breast. I immediately scheduled a mammogram, followed up with my doctors, and received a diagnosis of Stage 1 Ductal Carcinoma in Situ (DCIS) of the left breast."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            We're told she was diagnosed earlier this summer ... and had surgery to remove the growth.
      
    
            Mary, who recently executive produced a biopic on her life which aired on Lifetime earlier this year, tells us ... "Yes, hearing 'cancer' is scary, but there is also something incredibly important I want people to hear: I caught it early."
      

            According to Mary, paying attention to her body and taking action is what's allowed her to be proactive as far as getting treatment and healing.
      
    
            She says ... "I've walked through some incredibly difficult chapters in my life. I've survived things that I never imagined I would survive. And I have learned that life can change in an instant, but so can our perspective, our strength, and our ability to keep moving forward."
      
    
            Mary explained this is just another chapter of her story ... noting she's navigating it and is optimistic about her battle.
      
    
            She continued ... "And if there's one thing I've learned about myself after everything I've been through, it's this: I am a survivor, and I will survive this, too."
      
    
            As you know, Mary survived getting shot in the face in 1992 by a 17-year-old girl who was being sexually abused by Mary's then-husband.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Mary's urging people to take care of themselves, hoping her diagnosis will be a reminder to other women.
      
    
            She concluded ... "We spend so much time caring for the people we love, we have to remember to care for ourselves, too. Get your mammograms. Keep up with your screenings. Pay attention to changes in your body. And if something doesn't feel right, get it checked."
      
    
            We're told Mary is currently undergoing radiation therapy treatment ... and we're wishing her a full and speedy recovery.

            Alix Earle's stepmom is opening up about her involvement in the scandal surrounding former New York Governor Eliot Spitzer's resignation.
      
    
            Ashley Earle -- who went by Ashley Dupre -- got into the nitty-gritty of her escort days in a new piece for Elle.
      
    
            She wrote ... "At 19, while working as a cocktail waitress, a man approached me and told me I could make $1,000 an hour going on dates with high-profile men. My first answer was no, but I kept his card."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Ashley says she eventually gave the man a call, explaining she wanted money and independence.
      

            She said she spent 2 years as an escort without anyone in her life knowing when the FBI tracked her down and showed her a photograph of Spitzer -- who was her client.
      
    
            Ashley wrote ... "I didn't know who he was. When they told me he was the governor of New York, I couldn't begin to understand what was about to happen."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            She said it wasn't long before her stage name and face were in the tabloids, writing ... "I had come to New York City wanting to be noticed, and suddenly everyone noticed me -- for the one thing I never wanted anyone to know."
      
    
            Ashley says that for a while she wanted to clarify her identity and how she was perceived by giving the public context, but has since changed her tune.
      
    
            She says ... "Context isn't absolution. I made choices. Some were reckless. Some were selfish. They had consequences. I can own all of that without believing those choices have to be the most interesting thing about me forever."
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Ashley went on to explain that Alix's dad, TJ, was married when they met just a few months later, and that they "crossed a line we shouldn't have crossed."
      
    
            She owned up to hurting Alix, her sister Ashtin, and their mom, Alisa ... but justified it by saying her life with TJ is "deeply meaningful."
      
    
            Ashley said ... "I can acknowledge that the way our relationship began was complicated and caused pain without letting that define everything that came after it. Both things can exist at once."
